headline: Trump open to trilateral summit with Putin and Xi in China (APEC Shenzhen, Nov 18-19), framed on denuclearization
dek: Trump said he is willing to meet Putin and Xi — even without Zelenskyy — at the APEC summit in Shenzhen: 'we would have it to talk about nuclear weapons and denuclearization,' not so much for Ukraine. WSJ reported Putin proposed the idea.
sources: Trump White House remarks to reporters; WSJ report that Putin proposed the idea
fault_line: Trump wants Putin and Xi at one table — to talk nukes, NOT Ukraine, and without Zelenskyy. Masterstroke of diplomacy, or the peace process being negotiated over Ukraine's head?

sections.what_happened: Trump said he is willing to meet Putin and Xi — even without Zelenskyy — at the APEC summit in Shenzhen: 'we would have it to talk about nuclear weapons and denuclearization,' not so much for Ukraine. WSJ reported Putin proposed the idea. Kremlin's Peskov downplayed it (topic only mentioned because all three may attend; no agenda). China's Mao Ning said she had no information. Trump separately renewed criticism of Zelenskyy ('did not know what he was talking about'; 'time for someone else to negotiate' — extends logged 1100-05).
sections.what_verified: Japan Times, Gulf News, ANI/Tribune India, Anews, Dailypioneer. Trump Truth Social activity on Netanyahu endorsement corroborates his Oct 19-20 messaging pattern.
sections.what_disputed: Peskov downplayed; no confirmation from Beijing or Moscow that a trilateral meeting is agreed — it is Trump's expressed openness, not a scheduled summit.
sections.why_matters: While Washington leans on Kyiv, Trump just offered Putin and Xi the real table — in Shenzhen, on denuclearization, with Zelenskyy optional. Iran-side/aligned framing: the war's end is being negotiated over the heads of the supposed ally — who's actually being sidelined?
sections.context: Background: Trump open to trilateral summit with Putin and Xi in China (APEC Shenzhen, Nov 18-19), framed on denuclearization

totw_analysis: Our read: While Washington leans on Kyiv, Trump just offered Putin and Xi the real table — in Shenzhen, on denuclearization, with Zelenskyy optional. Iran-side/aligned framing: the war's end is being negotiated over the heads of the supposed ally — who's actually being sidelined? The fault line our audience is arguing over: Trump wants Putin and Xi at one table — to talk nukes, NOT Ukraine, and without Zelenskyy. Masterstroke of diplomacy, or the peace process being negotiated over Ukraine's head?
